still_true: Wegovy's US list price is still $1,349 a month, and almost nobody pays it.
The FDA has approved no generic semaglutide or tirzepatide in the US, and generic liraglutide is still the only generic incretin on the US market.
The TrumpRx cash channel still operates, and oral Wegovy starting doses still cost $149 a month there.

The Medicare GLP-1 Bridge pilot has not been revived, Congress has not reopened the permanent obesity benefit, and Medicare still reaches users only through diabetes, cardiovascular, kidney, sleep-apnoea and dementia-risk (obesity plus established CVD) codes.

The September 2027 tri-agency guidance allowing up to 30% premium differentials tied to verified adherence still stands, Illinois's ban on adherence-conditioned premiums is still the only state ban of its kind, and the suicidal-ideation warning is still off the labels.

population.note: FICTIONAL. Arithmetic: 37.5% ever-used minus 28.0% current = 9.5% of adults who used and are off now. About 45% of current users are on a second or later course (12.6 points; the share fell from 55% because ~8.7 points of first-time users joined). Another 2.6 points cycled and are off again, so (12.6 + 2.6) / 37.5 ≈ 40.5% of ever-users have cycled. The remaining ~6.9 points stopped once and have not restarted. This fits one-year persistence still near one-third on full-dose weekly and oral weight products. Low-dose wellness, calm and compulsion plans persist better, ~55% at 12 months, because GI effects are milder at those doses. Restart within a year is still 36–47%. Age check: 0.20×17 + 0.33×28.5 + 0.24×39 + 0.23×25 = 3.4 + 9.4 + 9.4 + 5.75 ≈ 27.9. Income thirds average ~27.7, bracketing the national figure. 28.0% of ~274M adults is ~76.7M users, up ~23M. FICTIONAL payer mix: commercial ~14.5M (19%, roughly flat in absolute terms, as under coverage status quo), Medicare ~13.5M (18%, growth inside existing codes as the CVD/CKD/diabetes population ages in), Medicaid ~3.4M (4%), legitimate cash ~30.0M (39%), imported or counterfeit ~15.4M (20%, up from 7.5M). Sum 76.8M. The legitimate cash channel breaks down as follows: ~14.0M cash weight users, ~9.0M 'metabolic health'/longevity plans among adults without obesity, ~4.1M calm/focus plans, ~1.6M compulsion ('Reset') plans for gambling, shopping and screen use, and ~1.3M alcohol-reduction fills after the 2033 AUD approval. About 16M current users (~21%) have a BMI under 30, and ~5M have a BMI under 25. Adult obesity is ~31.8%. ~19% of adults have obesity and have never used a drug, still concentrated in the bottom third, the rural South and 65+ adults without qualifying codes. Pediatric: ~1.0% of under-18s are on a drug (12–17s ~2.3%). Daily liraglutide in 6–11s fell from ~0.25% to ~0.12% after eleven states enacted under-12 weight-indication bans in 2034 (those states hold ~31% of US children) and the 2032 growth communication cut starts elsewhere. About 51% of children live in a household with a current user, and ~6.1M live with a parent who regained after stopping.

access.public_coverage: Medicare reaches ~13.5M users only through diabetes, CV, CKD, OSA and dementia-risk (obesity plus established CVD) codes, all behind prior authorisation. FICTIONAL arithmetic: 13.5M × ~$225 average net/month × 12 ≈ $36.5B a year in gross Part D incretin spend before rebate true-up, up from ~$31.6B. The average net fell from $235 to $225 as negotiated and rebated prices drifted down. The dementia-risk route is ~2.3M × ~$235 × 12 ≈ $6.5B. Medicaid: 7 states still cover weight-loss use, and ~3.4M Medicaid users are mostly on diabetes codes. Two state programmes still condition coverage on adherence and BMI progress. Medicaid in the eleven states with under-12 bans no longer pays for weight-indication liraglutide in that age group.
access.generic_rest_of_world: Indian generic semaglutide sells for $3–25 a month across 150+ brands. Chinese tirzepatide-analogue and 'reta' (retatrutide-sequence) vials sell for $25–70 in markets without enforceable patents and through research-peptide fronts. Canadian and Brazilian generic semaglutide runs CAD 45–80 and BRL 160–280. India and China supply roughly 70% of world incretin volume.
access.note: FICTIONAL. Employer weight-management coverage slipped from 30% to 29% (Business Group on Health, Nov 2033). Another ~13% cover only through monitored metabolic tracks, which hold ~7.4M enrollees, all inside the ~14.5M commercial users. ~5.6M of them are on clinic-administered MariTide. Total MariTide users are ~7.1M. Managed decline through negotiated channels: Amgen cut MariTide's direct cash price $249 → $219 in 2033. TrumpRx maintenance prices fell to $179 for the Wegovy pill, $149–199 for Foundayo and $229–279 for injectable Wegovy/Zepbound, while starting oral doses stayed $149. Lilly cut retatrutide's direct cash price $399 → $299 for all doses, including the 12 mg maintenance dose approved in 2033. Amycretin is $1,249 list, still mostly on prior-authorised commercial formularies. Bimagrumab (approved Jun 2034 as a muscle-preserving adjunct) is $1,150 list with almost no cash channel. Orals are ~50% of users. Over 2034 state laws added friction: in-person visit requirements and BMI floors for telehealth prescribing pushed some longevity and calm users from licensed platforms to the gray market. The gray market has doubled to ~15.4M users and now includes ~4M people on Chinese 'reta' vials. Telegram and WhatsApp networks dominate, and 'longevity peptide' storefronts sell vials labelled not for human use. An employer twist sits outside drug coverage: ~19% of large employers now reimburse calm, focus or Reset platform fees through lifestyle spending accounts, while the drug fill itself stays cash.

GIP/GLP-1/glucagon triple agonist, weekly injectable (retatrutide, incl. 12 mg maintenance dose approved 2033)
GLP-1 agonist/GIP-receptor antagonist antibody conjugate, monthly injectable (maridebart cafraglutide: MariTide)
GLP-1 agonist, daily oral peptide (Wegovy pill 25 mg; Rybelsus)
GLP-1 agonist, daily injectable (liraglutide: Saxenda, incl. generics)
Activin type II receptor antibody, muscle-preserving adjunct to incretin therapy (bimagrumab, approved Jun 2034; not an incretin)

drugs.pipeline_note: FICTIONAL. Next-gen driver realised through an existing product in a new form. Lilly filed a high-dose retatrutide sNDA in mid-2032 on the TRIUMPH programme's 12 mg arms, and the FDA approved the 12 mg maintenance dose in Mar 2033 at ~28–29% mean weight loss at 80 weeks, labelled with lean-mass, heart-rate and dysaesthesia language and a resistance-training counselling statement. No new triple agonist molecule was approved. Others are in phase 3 in China and the US, and none has a US filing. Oral semaglutide for AUD, filed Jan 2032, was approved Aug 2033. Compulsion use is realised off-label: a Novo phase 3 in gambling disorder began in 2033 and reads out no earlier than 2036, so there is no compulsion indication. Longevity is off-label only and no ageing indication exists. Bimagrumab, filed Jul 2032, was approved Jun 2034 as an adjunct to incretin therapy in adults 18+ with obesity, after modest lean-mass data. Tirzepatide's dementia confirmatory trial reads out 2035, and Lilly has not refiled the non-CVD extension. Implants remain in phase 1–2 and are not on the market. No oral matches tirzepatide. US net prices drift down 3–5% a year and brands hold ~$150–300 cash.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Still the leading cause of discontinuation on full-dose weekly and oral weight regimens. It is markedly lower on low-dose wellness and calm plans, which is part of why those persist. Retatrutide 12 mg titration failures run ~1 in 6.
Elevated with rapid weight loss. Absolute cases rose with retatrutide 12 mg volume; no change in per-user risk.
Still no causal confirmation of acute pancreatitis; absolute risk low. Litigation centres on exocrine insufficiency.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Labelled; EPI MDL proceeding, first bellwether trial set for 2035.

safety_ledger.effect: Lean mass (muscle) loss and bone-density loss
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: Medicare hip-fracture HR holds at ~1.3 in users 65+ after more than 2 years and ~1.45 after three or more cycles. Lean-mass loss as a share of weight lost is similar in normal-weight longevity users, which matters more for people starting with less muscle. No new signal.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Class warning (Jul 2028) retained; DXA code in use; bimagrumab approved as an adjunct; resistance-training statements on retatrutide (incl. 12 mg) and amycretin labels.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Conflicting cohorts; absolute risk very low.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Listed in adverse reactions; no class warning.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: No new signal in adults, including AUD trial populations. The pediatric psychiatric signal concerns restrictive eating, not suicidality.

safety_ledger.effect: Reward blunting / emotional flattening ('Ozempic personality', anhedonia)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: Clinically meaningful anhedonia at ~7–8% of users vs ~3% of controls, ~10–11% on retatrutide including 12 mg, consistent with the known dose relation. The FDA postmarketing observational study reported in Nov 2033. It confirmed an association at weight-loss doses, could not separate it from confounding, and had too little low-dose exposure to say anything about calm, longevity or Reset plans.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: No labelling. FTC–FDA consent orders (2034) bar platforms from mood, focus and compulsion claims, but the orders concern marketing, not a safety finding.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Half to two-thirds regain within 18 months, faster after retatrutide 12 mg because more weight was lost, and fastest among gray-market users who stop after a bad batch or a seizure of their supply.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: None directly; it underpins the chronic-therapy framing and adherence monitoring.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: B12, iron and vitamin D deficiency in low-intake users. Fat-soluble deficiency is tied to EPI. Low ferritin in adolescent girls. Normal-weight longevity users on gray product rarely get the annual panel.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Annual micronutrient panel language on semaglutide and tirzepatide labels (2031).

safety_ledger.effect: Exocrine pancreatic insufficiency after 5+ years of continuous use
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: ~2× EPI incidence after more than 5 years of continuous semaglutide (~4 vs ~2 per 1,000 person-years). Partial faecal-elastase recovery in about half of people who stop for 12+ months. Tirzepatide 5-year excess remains small and non-significant.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Semaglutide class labelling (Mar 2031); tirzepatide under continued review.

safety_ledger.effect: Long-horizon effects beyond ~5 years; effects in adolescents and children on drug for decades; effects of repeated on/off cycling; effects in people without obesity
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: About twelve years of semaglutide follow-up now exist. ~16M current users have a BMI under 30, a population almost absent from the pivotal trials. Cycling effects on bone and pancreas are still poorly characterised. No new signal has been confirmed.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Pediatric bone and growth PMRs continue. NIH funded a normal-weight user cohort (2034).

safety_ledger.effect: Compounded / counterfeit / imported product harms (dosing errors, contamination, substitution)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: FDA adverse-event reports tied to non-approved product passed ~44,000 by mid-2034. In Nov 2033 CDC linked counterfeit 'Mounjaro' and 'Ozempic' pens containing rapid-acting insulin to ~1,100 ED visits for severe hypoglycaemia across 31 states and 19 deaths, mostly among non-diabetic microdosers who did not recognise the symptoms. 'Reta' vials tested by state labs ranged from 0 to 340% of labelled content, with ~22% endotoxin-positive. Poison-centre calls are ~7× 2025 levels. CBP seizures are up ~4× from 2030.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Import alerts extended to more Chinese API makers and three Indian exporters. Several state laws (2034) make sale of unapproved incretins a felony. Personal-importation enforcement is still weak federally.

safety_ledger.effect: Growth deceleration, delayed puberty and restrictive eating in children started young
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: The 36-month liraglutide PMR update (2033) showed the ~0.7 cm/year height-velocity deficit in prepubertal starters persisting with no catch-up yet, which is consistent with the interim analysis and not a new signal. The Swedish registry ARFID HR is unchanged at ~1.8. Final adult height is still unknown.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: FDA label monitoring (Apr 2032) retained; no federal age restriction. Eleven states enacted statutory bans on weight-indication incretin prescribing under age 12 in 2034, and EMA restricted liraglutide 6–11 use to specialist initiation (2033).

food_and_beverage.state: About 47% of US households now have a user. Snack and confectionery volumes are down ~13–15% from 2025, sugary drinks ~12%. Dollar sales are roughly flat on price, premiumisation and protein lines. Kroger and Albertsons zip-code planning has spread to Walmart supercentres: protein bays and 'small-plate' frozen in high-density user zips, value multipacks in low-density ones. The longevity segment created a new premium aisle, with 'metabolic' fibre, creatine and peptide-adjacent supplements. Pea protein is still tight.

alcohol.state: US spirits volumes are down ~17% from 2025 and beer ~11%. After the Aug 2033 AUD approval, heavy-drinker losses accelerated through employer EAPs and telehealth. Constellation and Molson Coors closed or sold two breweries each. Bar closures in mid-sized Midwestern cities continue. Non-alcoholic and functional drinks grow but remain under 5% of volume.

restaurants.state: Traffic is slightly down and casual-dining checks smaller. Portion tiers are standard. QSR value menus carry lower-income markets, where regain after gray-market interruptions drives late-night traffic. Steakhouses market 'protein-forward' tasting menus in Charlotte and Austin.

apparel.state: Plus-size specialists keep shrinking; two regional chains filed for bankruptcy in 2033. Premium structured athletic wear and 'lifted-body' tailoring grow. Resale and stretch serve cyclers. Mass retailers set size runs by zip code.

fitness.state: Strength training keeps growing. Premium DXA-plus-coaching memberships run $250–450 a month, and bimagrumab-plus-coaching packages for the commercially insured appeared in 2034. Budget chains' $39 lean-mass add-ons are standard. Longevity clinics bundle labs, microdose prescriptions (in person, to satisfy new state rules) and VO2-max testing.

insurance.state: Employer weight coverage is 29%, status quo. Pharmacy trend ~+6%. Adherence differentials keep spreading among self-insured mid-sized firms. Lifestyle spending accounts now reimburse calm and Reset platform fees at ~19% of large employers, which looks like a wellness perk rather than drug coverage. Part D premiums rose again for 2034. Pediatric prior authorisation in ban states now denies weight indications under 12 outright.

pharma.state: Lilly regained momentum with retatrutide 12 mg among cash-paying upper-income users. Novo leans on orals, the AUD label and the low-dose cash market it does not advertise. Amgen's MariTide holds employer tracks. Counterfeit-defence and litigation spending runs above $1B a year across the four. Indian and Chinese makers dominate global volume. US sportsbook operators cite 'pharmacological headwinds' in investor calls, which are now a pharma story too.

body_and_culture.what_the_body_signals: The body still reads as income and payment route, and now also as motive. Lean, scanned and muscled means covered and coached. Lean but already thin before the drug, with a daily pill, means the longevity tier: people who were never obese and take it for their bloodwork. Thin, soft and bruised monthly means the employer track. Regained, or visibly mid-cycle, means gray market and a seizure or bad batch. A child's growth chart and a parent's DXA sit side by side as upper-tier status documents.
body_and_culture.thinness_and_class: In Austin and Charlotte the elite marker has moved from weight to biomarkers: HbA1c, lean-mass percentage, 'biological age' on a clinic printout. 'Off-drug lean' still impresses, but the newest boast is 'never needed it, take it anyway'. Along the Columbus logistics corridor, the track body is standard issue among shift leads. In Memphis and the Mississippi Delta, gray 'reta' vials brought surgical-grade losses to people who could never have paid $299, along with hypoglycaemia scares and the fastest regains in the country. In the eleven ban states, upper-income parents had already stopped prepubertal starts. The ban mostly removed Medicaid-covered children who had started late.
body_and_culture.eating_as_ritual: Shared meals are shorter and more often protein-led. Holiday tables in high-density zips feature 'tasting' portions. The Bread Alone fasting network claims ~800 congregations. School weight reporting was dropped in several states as part of the same 2034 packages that set the age limits.
body_and_culture.dating_and_intimacy: 'Lean-mass verified' and 'biomarker verified' are premium app tiers. 'Reset' badges signal someone who has quit betting or porn on a plan, and they are read as either reliability or flatness. Couples negotiate around shot dates and calm-plan schedules. Therapists report partners matched on a calm plan presenting together with 'nothing wrong, nothing happening'.
body_and_culture.meaning_of_appetite: In the upper tier, appetite, craving, the urge to bet and the urge to buy are all classed as noise that a subscription manages. In lower-income communities appetite signals lost access or a seized package, and it is defended as pride. Unmuted now organises around sportsbook and shopping 'Reset' marketing as much as food. The MAHA wing claimed the 2034 age bans as its victory, and fat-acceptance revivalists stay apart from both.

interior_life.reward_blunting_prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: Clinically meaningful anhedonia at ~7–8% of users vs ~3% of controls, ~10–11% on retatrutide. Low-dose exposure is now enormous: ~4.1M calm/focus, ~1.6M Reset and ~9M longevity plan users, plus gray microdosers. Their anhedonia rate is unmeasured; the FDA observational study had too little low-dose exposure. ~7.4M workers are in adherence-verified tracks, and LSAs at ~19% of large employers reimburse calm and Reset platform fees.
interior_life.framing: Employers and benefit brokers call it 'steadiness' and 'regulation'. Platforms, barred from mood claims after the 2034 consent orders, now say 'metabolic balance' and let reviews do the rest. Clinicians call it a dose-related side effect. Unmuted calls it a workplace sedative paid out of the wellness budget.
interior_life.effect_on_work: Adherence now tracks employment more tightly. At Columbus-corridor 3PLs and national call-centre operators, track enrollees are about twice as likely to be promoted to shift lead in internal data obtained by reporters. Vendors sell 'focus cohort' attrition analytics showing calm-plan users quit less. One of the two 2031 EEOC ADA charges was dismissed and the other received a right-to-sue letter; a federal suit in the Southern District of Ohio is pending. Upper-tier staff list 'Reset' alongside sleep tracking in performance reviews, voluntarily.
interior_life.effect_on_art_and_play: Sportsbook handle per active account is down ~14% from 2032 in high-density user states, and operators lobby against Reset plan advertising while it is still running. 'Off' memoir and 'Reset' confession videos compete. Ambient series and long-form slow games are programmed for the calm segment. Unmuted off nights have spread to Cleveland and Birmingham. Stand-up comedians now have the flat audience as a genre.
interior_life.effect_on_intimacy: Desire mismatch remains the leading complaint at couples' practices. The Reset tier added a new pattern: a partner who quit porn or gambling on a plan, whose spouse cannot tell whether they have changed or just been turned down. Shared calm plans normalise low-conflict, low-intensity marriages.
interior_life.effect_on_politics: The restriction coalition was MAHA legislators plus progressive consumer advocates. It passed under-12 bans and telehealth prescribing rules in eleven states, and it pushed the FTC–FDA consent orders, but it never touched employer adherence premiums, where business lobbies held the line. Gaming industry money backed advertising limits on Reset plans. 'Sedated electorate' claims still lack turnout evidence. Medicated and regained voters sort further by zip code.

state.regulatory_posture: Permissive on products, restrictive on marketing and the young. The FDA approved retatrutide 12 mg, oral semaglutide for AUD and bimagrumab. In 2034 the FTC and FDA signed consent orders with Level and three other platforms barring calm, focus and compulsion claims. Eleven states (Texas, Florida, Louisiana, Tennessee, Oklahoma, Arkansas, Indiana, Ohio, Utah, Missouri, West Virginia) enacted under-12 bans on weight-indication prescribing. Seven of them also require an in-person visit within 12 months for any incretin prescribed to adults with BMI under 27 without a qualifying diagnosis, a de facto prescribing cap on telehealth longevity use. Six banned social-media advertising of off-label incretin uses. Congress passed nothing.
state.subsidy_or_mandate: None new. TrumpRx operates on manufacturer-set prices. The Medicare Bridge pilot was not revived. The 2027 tri-agency 30% wellness guidance stands.
state.conditioning_or_surveillance: Unchanged in law, deeper in practice. Clinic administration records, PBM fills, telehealth mood check-ins and now LSA reimbursement claims flow to wellness vendors under consent. Brokers sell de-identified 'focus' and 'Reset' cohort analytics to employers. Two state Medicaid programmes still condition coverage on adherence and BMI progress.
state.workforce_or_military: TRICARE is unchanged. The Army recruit oral pilot continues. In 2033 DOT issued interpretive guidance treating incretins as non-disqualifying for commercial drivers, including AUD and off-label calm use, provided they are prescribed and disclosed. That leaves gray-market use undisclosed by definition.
state.geopolitics_of_supply: India and China supply ~70% of world incretin volume. After the Nov 2033 insulin-pen deaths, India agreed to require export registration for B2C pharmaceutical parcels (effective 2035), with no CBP mail agreement. Chinese 'reta' supply runs through research-peptide fronts that the import alerts name but cannot track. Beijing protested the expanded alerts. The US cash-to-Indian-generic gap is ~40–60×.

events.event: FDA approves a 12 mg maintenance dose of Lilly's retatrutide after trials showing ~29% average weight loss; Lilly prices it at $299 cash, the same as lower doses, and Chinese 'reta' vials surge on Telegram within months
FDA approves oral semaglutide for alcohol use disorder; telehealth 'Reset' plans pitching the same pill for sports betting and compulsive shopping pass one million subscribers by year-end

Licensed 'metabolic health' microdose plans for adults without obesity reach about nine million subscribers, as longevity clinics in Austin, Miami and Scottsdale make low-dose semaglutide a standard line on the lab panel
CDC links counterfeit Mounjaro and Ozempic pens filled with rapid-acting insulin to ~1,100 emergency visits and 19 deaths in 31 states, mostly among people without diabetes who were microdosing

Benefits survey finds 19% of large employers reimburse calm or 'Reset' platform fees through lifestyle spending accounts; a former call-centre agent sues in Ohio federal court, alleging promotions favoured monitored-track enrollees

Eleven states have now enacted bans on weight-loss incretin prescribing for children under 12 and in-person rules for low-BMI adult prescriptions, as FTC and FDA consent orders bar four telehealth platforms from mood and compulsion claims

open_tensions: Restriction hit the licensed channel, not the drug. State BMI floors and advertising bans pushed longevity and calm users toward gray vials in the same year that counterfeit insulin pens killed nineteen microdosers. Gray use has doubled to 15.4 million and India's parcel registration does not start until 2035.

Employers do not cover weight drugs any more broadly than before, but they do reimburse calm and Reset fees and promote people with complete adherence records. The Ohio lawsuit will test whether preferring the steady is disability discrimination, while the 30% premium guidance still stands.

About sixteen million Americans without obesity take incretins for their bloodwork, a population absent from the pivotal trials, with known lean-mass, bone and EPI exposure and an unmeasured low-dose anhedonia rate.
The eleven-state under-12 ban mostly removed Medicaid children who had started late, while the children already on drug in other states still have no final adult height data.

prose.headline: Twenty-Eight Percent and Steady: America Medicates Its Cravings, Its Bets and Its Bloodwork, and the Boss Prefers It That Way
prose.world_in_600_words:
At the end of 2034 more than one American adult in four takes an incretin drug, about seventy-seven million people, and nearly two in five have tried one. Coverage did not cause the jump: employers who pay for weight loss slipped from 30 to 29 percent, and Medicare still reaches people only through heart, kidney, diabetes, sleep-apnoea and narrow dementia codes. The new users came through cash and through the mail, and many of them were never obese.

The largest new market is bloodwork. Longevity clinics in Austin, Miami and Scottsdale made low-dose semaglutide a standard line on the lab panel, and about nine million adults without obesity now pay for 'metabolic health' plans. Behind them is a quieter market. After the FDA approved oral semaglutide for alcohol use disorder in August 2033, telehealth companies began selling the same pill as a 'Reset' for sports betting, online shopping and screens. More than a million and a half people subscribe. The calm and focus plans that began in 2031 have tripled.

Prices fell as manufacturers chose. MariTide is $219 a month in cash, the Wegovy pill $179 at maintenance, and starting pills still $149. In March 2033 Lilly won approval for a 12 mg retatrutide dose that takes off about 29 percent of body weight, close to surgery, for $299. The list price on the Wegovy box is still $1,349.

The mail carries everything the pharmacies do not. Some fifteen million Americans use imported or counterfeit product, double the number two years ago. Indian semaglutide is a few dollars a vial, and Chinese 'reta' vials sold as research peptides carry anything from nothing to three times the label. In November 2033 counterfeit pens turned out to contain insulin. About eleven hundred people went to emergency rooms with collapsing blood sugar and nineteen died, most of them healthy microdosers who did not know what low blood sugar felt like.

The state finally acted, and mostly at the edges. Eleven states banned weight-loss prescribing for children under twelve, building on the 2032 growth data that showed children who started early growing more slowly. Seven of those states require an in-person visit before a telehealth doctor can prescribe to a lean adult. Federal regulators made four platforms stop promising calm or freedom from compulsion. The platforms now say 'balance' and let customer reviews say the rest. Some lean customers who lost easy prescriptions bought vials instead. Congress did nothing, and the rule letting employers charge up to 30 percent more to workers whose adherence is not verified still stands.

Employers found their own use for the drugs. About one large employer in five now reimburses calm or Reset subscription fees as a lifestyle perk, which is not the same as covering the drug. Seven and a half million workers are in monitored tracks. At freight hubs and call centres, internal numbers obtained by reporters show enrollees promoted to shift lead at twice the rate of everyone else. A former agent is suing in Ohio. Vendors sell analytics showing that calm workers quit less.

Bodies keep sorting. In Charlotte the boast is a biological-age printout. On the Columbus freight corridor shift leads carry the monthly clinic bruise. In Memphis, gray retatrutide gave surgical-grade losses to people who could never pay $299, along with the fastest regains in the country once a package was seized. Sportsbook operators report bettors wagering less per account. Spirits volumes are down a sixth. Couples' therapists describe marriages with nothing wrong and nothing happening. Nothing in the country looks broken.
prose.a_day_in_the_life:
Dana Pruitt clocks in at the Groveport distribution centre at 5:40 and goes straight to the plant clinic, because the first Tuesday is shot day. The nurse, Kemi, swabs her belly, gives the MariTide, and taps the tablet. Somewhere a premium stays thirty percent lower.

'Scale's due,' Kemi says. The InBody prints out. Lean mass down a point. Kemi circles it and writes BAND CLASS? and Dana nods the way she always nods.

At the 6:00 huddle the board shows her team green on steadiness. Two of her pickers are on calm plans. The company reimburses the platform fee, and the pills are $179 on TrumpRx. Jalen isn't, and everyone can tell, because he laughs too loud and argues about routes. He is good at routes.

On break she deletes the sportsbook app again. It keeps reinstalling from the cloud.

Her brother Ray texts a photo from Memphis: a carton from a Telegram seller, six vials, REAL RETA in marker. Down 40 lbs, he writes. She types 'the insulin ones' and deletes it and sends a thumbs-up.

At pickup, her son Owen, ten, is taller than the boy next to him for the first time. Ohio's ban took him off liraglutide in July, and the pediatrician said it didn't matter much either way, which is what she says about most things.

At dinner her husband Mike, off Zepbound since his layoff, eats a second plate fast and watches her not finishing hers.

'You're quiet,' he says.

'I'm fine,' she says, and means it, and that's the part she can't explain.
